A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenHancer work. All 17 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-G, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP and MLLM benchmark experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendices D-F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, global-token conditioning, LoRA updates, and continuous and discrete denoisers remain unchanged. Appendix G retains the same two algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use CC3M for training and the same vision-centric, general multimodal, classification and retrieval benchmarks. No dataset, task or appendix test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Original CLIP and DIVA remain comparators in the same experiments, and the pre-trained FLUX.1-dev efficiency comparison is retained. The newly cited DEEM work is not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The six CLIP backbone configurations, Vicuna-7B/13B evaluations, metrics, training budgets and evaluation procedures remain identical in Section 5 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The conditional-token, training-stage, timestamp, denoiser-size, LoRA, Stage-2 updating and mask-ratio analyses are unchanged. Appendices E-F retain the same qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outcomes are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same MMVP-VLM averages for OpenAICLIP@224: 25.9 for DIVA and 31.9 for GenHancer.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof, the mutual-information decomposition and regularization argument, and Equations 1-7 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about imperfect reconstruction, lightweight two-stage enhancement, applicability to continuous and discrete denoisers, and improved vision-centric performance.

C2.justification: Explanations involving local-token information leakage, irrelevant information and smaller SigLIP improvements remain unchanged, as do the appendix interpretations. No substantive limitation or qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is unchanged, including learning rates, batch size, eight-GPU training, LoRA settings, appendix pseudocode and the project/code access statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds Luo et al.'s DEEM: Diffusion models serve as the eyes of large language models for image perception as reference 31, citing it in Section 2's existing data-augmentation sentence. Existing references and substantive comparisons with prior work are retained.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to the added citation and bibliography entry, consequent reference renumbering, and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Substantive prose and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference slightly reflows Section 2 and the bibliography across pages 10-11. Figures 1-11 and Tables 1-8 retain their visual content, structure and placement, apart from citation-number updates.

improvement.justification: v2 adds one related-work citation without expanding its discussion or revising the paper's methods, evidence, explanations or reproducibility information. This limited bibliographic update and accompanying reflow produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
